Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Routing delay spike observed — need triage

Team,

We observed a sudden uptick in routing-induced per-request latency affecting a subset of customers (notably FastLane Commerce) starting ~08:45 PT. p95 for gen-api increased from ~420ms -> ~1.3s for requests that hit cross-region routing. KPIs: sustained QPS unchanged, but tail latency and time-to-first-byte rose.

Initial findings:
- Spike correlates with autoscaler churn on eu-west pool; some requests got routed to fallback GPU hosts with higher cold-start latency.
- KV cache hit rates are stable; not seeing cache eviction signals.
- No obvious error budget burn (errors < 0.1%), but latency SLOs breached for affected routes.

Immediate asks:
1) Marcus / Eng: can you triage routing decisions and confirm whether the autoscaler misfired on region tag? If we can pin to configuration, consider an immediate conservative rollout pause.
2) Marissa / Product: please advise on whether we should pause the rollout that changed routing weights last night (v2 routing-scheduler).
3) Lauren / CS: we should prepare a brief customer message for FastLane explaining we see transient latency and outlining mitigation steps.

Attachments: p95_spike_graph.png (engine summary graph, p95 timeline)

I'm standing by in #incident-routing with logs and the quick query.

- Soojin
Soojin Lee | SRE
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: soojin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Routing delay spike observed — need triage

Thanks Soojin — quick update from triage:
- Autoscaler logs show multiple scale-down events between 08:40-08:46 that overlapped with traffic bursts. The routing-scheduler applied fallback routing to older host groups which have longer warmup. This looks like a scheduling decision rather than model-level perf regression.
- Short-term mitigation: pining routing to the primary eu-west pool for affected customers and draining the fallback group. I can push a conservative override in 15m; will monitor p95.

Product question for Marissa: last night's release to routing-scheduler bumped the smoothing window from 30s->10s. Was that intentional for latency sensitivity? If so, it increased churn sensitivity. If we can't revert quickly, suggest reverting smoothing window and add a temporary guard to avoid cross-region fallback for tiered customers.

Lauren: if you can get signoff on a customer note we can apply the override and message concurrently.

Attachments: (none)

- Marcus
Marcus Lin | Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Rajiv —

We’re reaching out because our telemetry shows transient increases in request latency impacting a small percentage of requests to your account this morning (May 17, ~08:45 PT). We’ve identified the cause as an internal routing decision that routed a fraction of traffic to warmup hosts, which increased tail latency for the affected requests.

What we’re doing now:
- We’re applying a conservative routing override to pin traffic to the primary eu-west pool for FastLane while we stabilize the scheduler. (ETA: ~30 minutes)
- We will pause the recent routing-scheduler smoothing window change until we have more confidence in behavior.
- We will share a short post-incident note with timelines and mitigations by EOD.

What you can expect:
- Short-term latency improvement within ~30 minutes of override.
- Follow-up with a summary and any configuration changes we make.

If you can share any examples (request IDs or screenshot) of recent slow responses it will help diagnostics — attaching a stub below where you can drop files.

Attachment: customer_note_draft.md (internal draft).

Would appreciate quick signoff or edits from Soojin/Marcus/Marissa; I’ll send once we have alignment.

Thanks,

Team — closing the loop on this one. Summary of actions taken and owners: 

Timeline:
- 2027-05-17 08:45 PT — p95 spike observed (SRE/telemetry)
- 09:00 PT — Marcus deployed a conservative routing override pinning traffic to eu-west primary pool
- 09:40 PT — observed p95 reduce back to baseline (~440ms) for affected routes
- 10:05 PT — Drafted and sent customer note; Rajiv confirmed receipt and asked about ordering implications

What we told the customer (FastLane): short explanation of routing fallback and mitigation, ETA for fix, and a promise of an EOD post-incident note. Rajiv asked about retries/ordering; Marcus confirmed the override does not change request ordering or retry semantics.

Open items / Product asks:
- Marissa: please track the routing-scheduler smoothing window revert as a P0 in the serving roadmap; we need a guard that prevents <60s smoothing windows for accounts with cross-region constraints.
- Marcus: add a canary check to detect autoscaler churn -> fallback routing events and fire a lightweight alert so ops can pause rollouts earlier.
- Soojin: please attach the incident query and sample request IDs to the post-incident note (link in related_links).

I've emailed the finalized customer summary and copied Rajiv. Posting the post-incident doc to the incident page now: https://docs.redwood.com/incident/2027-05-17-routing-delay

Closing note: no SLA credit requested by customer at this time — keep monitoring and flag if FastLane notices any recurrence.

Thanks all for fast turnaround.

— Lauren
